sections.name: JURISDICTION
sentences: Jurisdiction of this Court comes under 28 U.S.C. Sec. 1331 (Federal Question) based on Plaintiff's claims under Title VII. The state law components of this action arise under the PHRA.
This Court has supplemental subject matter jurisdiction over the state law components of this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. Section 1367(a).

sections.name: PROCEDURAL REQUIREMENTS
sentences: On or about 8/5/2024, within 300 days of the occurrence of the acts of discrimination of which she complains, Plaintiff Lesly Flores filed a Charge against her employer with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”) alleging sex-based employment discrimination.
Said Charge was concurrently filed with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission.
The EEOC has held exclusive jurisdiction over Plaintiffs Complaint.
Case 2:25-cv-01738-MSG Document1 Filed 04/04/25 Page 6of13 To date the EEOC has not reached a conciliation agreement to which Plaintiff is a party.

On March 26, 2025 Plaintiff received from the EEOC a Notice of Right To Sue, allowing her to sue in Federal Court within ninety (90) days. (See attached hereto and incorporated herein as Plaintiff's Exhibit “A”, Notice of Right To Sue letter dated March 26, 2025.).

sections.name: FACTS
sentences: On or about February 6, 2023 Plaintiff Lesly Flores, a female, was hired by Defendant Saint Joseph’s University as a Public Safety employee at its campus located at 5600 City Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19131.
Defendant is a university with residential, administrative, academic, athletic, and recreational facilities located at the above campus.

Plaintiff's duties included, but were not limited to, providing security on the campus and in the facilities Beginning immediately after her hire, a superior male co-worker of Plaintiff's, Ron Morman, began sexually harassing Plaintiff.
This sexual harassment began as Mr. Morman was training Plaintiff during her probationary period.
Mr. Moorman would show Plaintiff pornographic videos.
Mr. Moorman constantly would hug and kiss Plaintiff against her will.
Mr. Moorman would touch himself inappropriately in front of Plaintiff.
Mr. Moorman would constantly make unwanted sexual advances towards Plaintiff.

Plaintiff would consistently remove herself from Mr. Moorman’s presence and rebuke his above behavior, but his behavior persisted. | Mr. Moorman’s above unwanted sexual harassment continued throughout 2023 and into This harassment included Mr. Morman texting and calling Plaintiff on her cell phone and expressing romantic interest in her and propositioning her, including but not limited to a call on March 27, 2024.

On March 28, 2024 Plaintiff verbally confronted Mr. Morman about his conduct in the Lo Case 2:25-cv-01738-MSG Document1 Filed 04/04/25 Page 7of13 ) presence of a dispatcher Martina (Inu), Plaintiff's superior.
Again no steps were taken to remedy the situation and the harassment continued.

Plaintiff reported Mr. Moorman’s sexual harassment to management, including, but not limited to, Plaintiff's supervisor Jackie Franco and supervisor Saulman Byrd. or, Co-workers Michael Howard, Mike Lupton, and others were also made aware of this sexual harassment.
Despite its knowledge of the above and Plaintiff's resultant distress, no disciplinary or preventative action whatsoever was ever taken by management here.
After the above March 27, 2024 incident and others when Plaintiff would rebuke him, Mr. Morman would speak badly of Plaintiff to her co-workers and management, causing her further distress.
30, Plaintiff's last day of employment with Defendant was June 16, 2024.
Defendant by and through its employees humiliated, embarrassed, and subjected Plaintiff to mental distress and anguish through its deliberate sexual harassment.
The harassment here was severe and pervasive and caused Plaintiff great emotional harm.
Plaintiff sought and received medical treatment for her mental distress and anguish.

sections.name: COUNT I
sentences: Title VII - Sex Discrimination in Employment (Sexual Harassment - Hostile Work Environment) Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs | through 33 as though set forth in full herein.
By the conduct set forth in the Statement of Facts above, Defendant engaged in unlawful employment discrimination in violation of Section 703 (a) of Title VII, 42 U.S.C. Section 2000e- 2(a).

Taken together, the acts outlined above describe a pattern of intentional discrimination against and disparate treatment of Plaintiff on account of her gender (female) with respect to the terms and conditions of her employment.
Taken together, the acts outlined above constitute a hostile work environment based on gender.

Case 2:25-cv-01738-MSG Document1 Filed 04/04/25 Page 8of13 (a) Plaintiff suffered the intentional discrimination outlined above because of her membership in a protected class - female. (b) Such discrimination was severe, pervasive, and regular. (c) Such discrimination detrimentally affected Plaintiff. (d) Such discrimination would have detrimentally affected a reasonable person of the same protected class in her position. (e) There existed in the corporate Defendant respondeat superior liability for the actions of its agents and employees. (f) Defendant failed to exercise reasonable care to prevent and correct promptly any harassment.
The unlawful employment practices outlined above were intentional.
As a result of Defendant’s actions and conduct Plaintiff has suffered emotional distress, mental anguish, and loss of enjoyment of life’s pleasures.

The above described acts and omissions of Defendant with regard to Plaintiff were egregious and were committed with a malicious, willful, and/or reckless indifference to the Federally protected rights of Plaintiff.
Al. Said acts and omissions of Defendant were committed by and through its employees within their agency relationships with Defendant.
The extreme and outrageous acts and omissions of Defendant merit the imposition of punitive damages.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff Lesly Flores prays that this Court: (a) accepts jurisdiction over this matter; (b) impanels and charges a jury with respect to the causes of action; and (c) awards the following damages: punitive, liquidated, and compensatory damages including, but not limited to, damages for pain and suffering, anxiety, humiliation, and emotional distress in order to compensate her for the injuries she has suffered and to signal to other employers that such acts in employment are repulsive to legislative enactments and public policy; il. attorneys’ fees, expert witness fees, and the costs of this action; ill. any other relief which this Court deems just and equitable.
